midband_extended.description: Phase 2: is treat_midband_pool's win (bal.acc 0.9336 vs reference 0.9248, best on every metric measured) real and worth building on? Three questions. (1) Robustness: a second seed, and three tuning variants of the band/pool that bracket the winning (0.35,0.9)/pool=128 config -- narrower (0.5,0.8), wider (0.2,0.95), and a bigger pool (256) at the same band -- to see whether the win is a knife-edge or a genuine basin. (2) Fairness: treat_midband_pool's own worst-group accuracy (0.748) trails three lower-overall-accuracy arms, so this tests two concrete fixes. treat_midband_perf_group and treat_fair_weight_only introduce a new signal -- GroupPerformanceTracker, tracking REALISED per-group running error (not predicted I-value, which this project's own gate result shows barely correlates with realised outcomes) -- used respectively to restrict the candidate pool to the worst-performing groups (the selection-side idea) and to multiply loss weight by relative group error (the weighting-side idea, composable with any --ivalue-loss-weight mode including 'none'). treat_midband_group is the cheap comparison point: the EXISTING I-value-based group_targeting composed with midband, zero new code. treat_fair_weight_only is the clean control: fairness weighting alone, i.i.d. sampling, no I-value involved at all. (3) Distribution: does the win hold under a demographically-balanced training set (--fair-train, the closest thing to a 'fair dataset' the project already builds), and under leave-one-out generalisation (--holdout H1_diffusion_unseen, the project's headline holdout)? All ten arms otherwise match treat_midband_pool exactly -- same architecture, epochs, node budget -- so a run differs from it in exactly the one dimension its name says.
